title: On Catastrophic Inheritance of Large Foundation Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated through a literature review of real-world case studies, such as citing incidents where text-to-image models generated lighter skin and blue eyes when prompted for a 'professional' headshot, and reviewing existing research on models propagating race-based medicine.

Reviewed by citing existing empirical studies that demonstrate performance disparities, such as a documented 18.12% accuracy reduction in GPT-3.5 when answering non-English medical questions compared to English queries.

Synthesizes findings from existing research to theoretically analyze how foundation models inherit harmful stereotypes, cultural dominance, and gender biases from uncurated, large-scale web data containing unethical content.

Theoretically analyzes and reviews existing literature showing how long-tailed distributions and class imbalances in pre-training datasets skew model capabilities, resulting in worse performance for rare or underrepresented visual and textual concepts.
